questions.question_text:
Seven persons A, B, C, M, N, P, and R are of different heights. C is taller than B, who is taller than both N and A. R is taller than both N and M. The number of persons taller than N is the same as those shorter than N. B is shorter than R, who is not the tallest person. Only two person heights between B and P, who is taller than M.
Q10. How many persons’ heights are between R and P?
questions.explanation: The unique low-to-high order is M, P, A, N, B, R, C. A, N and B lie between P and R, so there are three.
questions.source: Order and Ranking 01  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 10

Q11. Who among the following persons is the third tallest?
questions.explanation: In the unique low-to-high order M, P, A, N, B, R, C, the third tallest is B.
questions.source: Order and Ranking 01  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 11

questions.question_text:
A, B, C, D, P, Q, and R are seven friends. Each has a different height. There are two friends whose heights are between Q and R, with Q taller than those friends but shorter than R. Q is not the shortest. Only two friends are taller than C. A is taller than D but shorter than B, who is not the tallest. Not more than four people are shorter than B. P is not the second tallest.
How many people are taller than B?
questions.explanation: The unique order from shortest to tallest is D, A, Q, B, C, R, P. C, R and P are taller than B: three people.
questions.source: Order and Ranking 01  Class Notes.pdf, physical p. 13

questions.question_text:
Six persons A, B, C, D, E and F have different heights. Each person likes a different colour—Red, Blue, White, Pink, Yellow and Grey. The person who likes Pink is not the tallest. The person who likes Blue is taller than C but shorter than the person who likes Pink. F is shorter than the person who likes Pink but taller than the person who likes Blue. F likes Red. B is taller than the person who likes Yellow but shorter than F. The person who likes Yellow is taller than E. A likes neither Pink nor Grey. The second tallest is 150 cm and the third lowest is 60 cm.
If the sum of the heights of D and F is 290 cm, what is the possible height of F?
questions.explanation: The unique ordering is E, C, B, F, D, A from shortest to tallest. D is second tallest at 150 cm, so F=290−150=140 cm.
questions.source: Order and Ranking 01  Class Notes.pdf, physical pp. 15–16
